title: Introduce migration simulation engine and terraform plan quarantine
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a migration simulation engine (rwi-migrate simulate) for dry-run verification; introduces a terraform 'plan quarantine' stage and S3 lockfile gating; Helm pre-upgrade and post-restore hooks for quorum validation; admission webhook to block CRD downgrades; operator annotations for quarantine/rollback optimization; CLI flags for dry-run migrations and restore validation. No breaking changes to public APIs; opt-in features for Private deployments.
description:
Context and motivation:
This PR addresses a recurring pattern we saw during private deploy upgrades: plan/apply drift during tenant migrations, accidental downgrade attempts against pinned CRD revisions, and high-impact restores that surface missing post-restore validations. The goal is to give operators a safe place to run realistic upgrade/restore simulations and to gate Terraform/Helm applies when the migration plan may have cross-component impacts.

What this PR introduces (high level):
- Migration Simulation Engine (rwi-migrate simulate): an operator-agnostic local simulator that replays state snapshots and a sampled set of API interactions to detect non-idempotent migrations and common schema-compatibility regressions. Works in dry-run mode and can produce a reenactment report.
- Terraform Plan Quarantine: a small Terraform module and wrapper that writes a plan lockfile to the configured S3 backend (plan-quarantine/<run-id>.lock). When a quarantine file is present and not acknowledged via the console/CLI, subsequent applies are blocked by CI/automation hooks.
- Helm hooks: added pre-upgrade-quarantine and post-restore-validate hooks in the private-installer chart. pre-upgrade-quarantine pauses operator scaling and takes a live snapshot; post-restore-validate runs a lightweight validation job against the restored DB and KV stores.
- CRD version pinning + downgrade admission webhook: CRDs gain an optional annotation 'redwood.io/upgrade-safe: vX' to indicate minimum supported operator version. An admission webhook denies downgrade attempts that would violate annotations.
- Restore concurrency limiter and rollback optimizer: default restore concurrency reduced to 2 for private clusters; added algorithm to compute a minimal-rollback-set based on tenant dependency graph to reduce blast radius during rollbacks.
- Vault/KMS snapshot encryption integration: simulation engine can optionally decrypt snapshots using configured Vault path to replay encrypted backups locally.

- charts/private-installer/templates/hooks/pre-upgrade-quarantine-job.yaml (new)
- charts/private-installer/templates/hooks/post-restore-validate-job.yaml (new)

Review conversation (high level):
- Diego Martinez (review): "Nice work — the quarantine pattern will reduce human error during large upgrades. A couple of asks: add an index on the snapshot metadata table for replay speed; make the default quarantine TTL 72h. Also please show how plan-quarantine interacts with existing TF state locks."
- Author (Maya): "Added index and bumped TTL to 72h; expanded TF docs to call out how the S3 quarantine lock is orthogonal to the TF state lock and the recommended order is: run plan -> write quarantine -> manual review -> acknowledge -> apply. See docs/private-deploy/plan-quarantine.md."
- Priya Nambiar (review): "Concern about admission webhook latency and race conditions during canary rollouts."
- Author (Maya): "Webhook runs a cheap annotation check and caches CRD version hints for 10s; documented behavior and added metrics. We avoid full CRD deserialization during admission to keep p95 under 30ms in our tests."
- Ethan Shaw (request changes): "e2e flaky — please isolate and mark nightly. Also add CI gate that prevents merging unless e2e passes in nightly for 48h."
- Author (Maya): "Moved the test to nightly, added a feature-flagged gate in ci/policy (requires 48h green on nightly for merge), and added a follow-up PR placeholder in the release notes."
- Diego Martinez (approval): "LGTM — approved after e2e moved to nightly and docs updated."

CI summary:
- unit: pass (all packages)
- integration: pass (helm template, terraform plan smoke)
- e2e (PR): one flaky test failed on first run (migration_sim_replay_test.go) — retried in CI, passed on rerun; test marked as nightly-only going forward
- lint: pass

Backward-compatibility and safety notes:
- All changes are opt-in for existing private installs. The admission webhook is installed behind a feature flag for 2 release cycles and will not block existing clusters unless enabled. The terraform quarantine module is additive and must be wired into customer CI pipelines to take effect.

Operational playbook excerpts (added to docs/private-deploy/playbooks.md):
- How to run a full migration simulation: 'rwi-migrate simulate --snapshot s3://<bucket>/snapshots/<id> --sample-tenants 50 --out report.json'
- How to acknowledge and lift a quarantine: 'rwi-quarantine ack <run-id> --operator <email>' (this signals console and writes ack file to S3)
- Restore flow with validation: pre-upgrade-quarantine job runs -> operator acknowledges -> apply -> post-restore-validate runs -> if validation fails, rollback optimizer suggests minimal rollback set and 'rwi-rollback plan' can be used to preview restore set

notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: quarantine is opt-in, admission webhook behind feature flag, nightly-only e2e for replay. Designed to reduce blast-radius for private upgrades.
